items.title: Trump says US seized Iranian ship as talks falter

featured_image.name: US Navy Seizes Iranian-Flagged Cargo Ship in Gulf of Oman ...

items.description: President Donald Trump announced on Sunday that American forces had captured an Iranian-flagged cargo vessel near the Strait of Hormuz, escalating tensions just as Washington pushes to restart stalled peace negotiations with Tehran. Hours later, Iran rejected the proposed second round of talks, casting fresh doubt on the prospects for a diplomatic resolution before a fragile ceasefire expires on Wednesday.

items.title: Iran refuses to negotiate while US naval blockade remains in place

featured_image.name: US general clarifies Iranian ports under blockade, not Strait of Hormuz

items.description: Iran has declared it will not send a negotiating delegation to Pakistan for a second round of peace talks with the United States as long as a US naval blockade of its ports remains in effect, according to Iran's semi-official Tasnim news agency on Sunday. The announcement throws into doubt a planned resumption of diplomacy just days before a fragile ceasefire is set to expire on April 22.[1][2][3][4]

items.title: Iran refuses to send negotiators to Pakistan over US naval blockade

featured_image.name: Iran closes Strait of Hormuz again over US blockade of its ports

items.description: Iran has declared it will not send a negotiating delegation to Pakistan for a second round of peace talks with the United States as long as a US naval blockade of its ports remains in place, according to reports from Iran's semi-official Tasnim news agency on Sunday. The refusal throws into doubt plans announced by President Donald Trump, who said his representatives would arrive in Islamabad on Monday evening to resume negotiations.[1][2][3][4][5]

items.title: Trump reverses course, confirms Vance will lead Iran talks in Pakistan

featured_image.name: Vance, Witkoff, Kushner are in negotiations with Iran in Pakistan

items.description: In a confusing sequence of announcements on Sunday, President Donald Trump initially told ABC News that Vice President JD Vance would not travel to Pakistan for a second round of negotiations with Iran, only for the White House to later confirm that Vance would in fact lead the delegation. The back-and-forth unfolded as the administration scrambled to arrange talks ahead of a fragile ceasefire set to expire on Wednesday.

items.title: Pope Leo XIV prays at Angola shrine tied to slave trade

featured_image.name: TOPSHOT-ANGOLA-VATICAN-DIPLOMACY

items.description: Pope Leo XIV on Sunday led a rosary prayer at the Sanctuary of Mama Muxima, a revered Catholic shrine in Angola built by Portuguese colonizers in the late 16th century that served as a hub in the transatlantic slave trade. The visit marked one of the most symbolically charged moments of the American pope's 11-day tour of Africa.[1][2]

items.title: Trump sends envoys to Pakistan for new Iran talks

featured_image.name: Pakistan proposes second round of U.S.-Iran talks as standoff ... - PBS

items.description:
President Donald Trump announced Sunday that White House envoys Steve Witkoff and Jared Kushner are heading to Islamabad for a second round of direct negotiations with Iran, with talks set to begin Tuesday, as the ceasefire between Washington and Tehran approaches its April 22 expiration.[1][2]

In an interview with Fox News, Trump warned that if Tehran does not agree to a deal, the whole of Iran will be "blown up," specifically threatening to target bridges and power plants. He demanded that Iran reopen the Strait of Hormuz and surrender its highly enriched uranium stockpile.[2][1]

items.title: U.S. backs $50M rare earth project in South Africa to cut China reliance

featured_image.name: US backs a South Africa project to extract rare earths as it ... - AP News

items.description: A U.S.-backed project in South Africa aims to extract rare earth minerals from massive industrial waste dunes, part of a broader push by Washington to loosen China's grip on the critical minerals supply chain.

items.title: Iran regains 60% of missile launchers during ceasefire, US intelligence estimates

featured_image.name: Iran reportedly recovering bombed missile bunkers within ...

items.description: Seven weeks after the United States and Israel launched Operation Epic Fury against Iran, American intelligence and military officials now estimate that Tehran still holds roughly 60 percent of its pre-war missile launchers and about 40 percent of its long-range attack drone arsenal, according to a report by The New York Times published on Friday. The assessment underscores a widening gap between the Trump administration's claims of having devastated Iran's military and the reality on the ground.[1][2][3]

items.title: Penn State develops 3D-printed brain sensors tailored to each patient

featured_image.name: Penn State researchers develop 3D printed bioelectrodes ...

items.description: Researchers at Penn State have unveiled a method for 3D printing soft, stretchable brain electrodes customized to the unique folds of each patient's brain, a development that could reshape how neurological diseases are monitored and treated.

items.title: French peacekeeper killed as Lebanon ceasefire frays

featured_image.name: In southern Lebanon, UN peacekeepers are caught in a vice

items.description: Israeli forces continued shelling and demolition operations across southern Lebanon on Saturday, less than two days after a US-brokered 10-day ceasefire took effect, raising doubts about the durability of the truce even as a French UN peacekeeper was killed in a separate attack attributed to Hezbollah.

items.title: Iran calls free transit through Hormuz 'a fiction' as Europe plans naval mission

featured_image.name: Why are some ships going through the Strait of Hormuz during ...

items.description: Iran pushed back forcefully against European calls to reopen the Strait of Hormuz on Saturday, even as dozens of countries gathered in Paris a day earlier to plan a multinational naval mission to restore free passage through one of the world's most critical shipping lanes.

items.title: North Korea fires ballistic missile into East Sea

featured_image.name: Report: North Korea conducts new missile test from warship - Yahoo

items.description:
North Korea launched at least one ballistic missile eastward on Sunday, South Korea's Joint Chiefs of Staff confirmed, in the latest in a rapid succession of weapons tests that have heightened tensions across the Korean Peninsula this year.[1][2]

The JCS said it detected the missile launch and was analyzing details of the firing, including its range and flight characteristics. The AFP, citing Yonhap, reported that the South Korean military had tracked the missile heading toward the East Sea, also known as the Sea of Japan.[2][3]

items.title: Iran recloses Strait of Hormuz, deepening jet fuel crisis

featured_image.name: Jet fuel shortage: Why Iran war could ground flights in Europe

items.description: The war in Iran has pushed the global aviation industry to a breaking point, with jet fuel prices nearly doubling since the conflict began and airlines across Europe, Asia, and North America now canceling flights and grounding aircraft as supplies dwindle.

items.title: Trump Organization plans 70-story tower in Tbilisi, Georgia

featured_image.name: The Trump company is not banning private foreign deals, a break ...

items.description:
The Trump Organization is planning to build a roughly 70-story luxury residential tower in Tbilisi, Georgia, a project that would become the tallest building in the country's capital and mark the family business's latest international venture during Donald Trump's second term in office.

The Wall Street Journal first reported the project on Friday, with Reuters confirming that "Trump Tower Tbilisi" will be a mixed-use development branded by the Trump Organization in partnership with local developers. Details about the specific Georgian partners involved, the project's estimated cost, and its expected timeline have not yet been fully disclosed.[1][2]

items.title: Iran fires on Indian-flag ships after reclosing Hormuz strait

featured_image.name: Firing on Indian ships in Hormuz reveals who wields real power in Iran

items.description: Iran's Revolutionary Guards reversed the country's decision to reopen the Strait of Hormuz on Saturday, reimposing restrictions on the critical waterway and firing on two Indian-flagged vessels attempting to pass through — a sharp escalation that deepened uncertainty over global energy supplies as the 49th day of the U.S.-Iran war drew to a close.

items.title: U.S. prepares to board Iran-linked ships worldwide

featured_image.name: The US is ready to seize Iran-linked ships with boarding ...

items.description:
The U.S. military is preparing to board Iran-linked oil tankers and seize commercial vessels in international waters within the coming days, the Wall Street Journal reported Saturday, marking a sharp expansion of the naval pressure campaign against Tehran beyond the Middle East.[1][2][3]

The move comes as the Trump administration's Operation Economic Fury enters a new phase, extending enforcement of the naval blockade of Iranian ports — now in its sixth day — to a global maritime pursuit of vessels tied to Iran's oil trade. A temporary ceasefire between Washington and Tehran is set to expire next week.[2][3]

items.title: NATO chief Rutte calls US withdrawal speculation 'absurd'

featured_image.name: Mark Rutte takes up position as head of NATO

items.description:
NATO Secretary General Mark Rutte has pushed back against growing speculation that the United States could leave the alliance, declaring in an interview published by German newspaper Welt am Sonntag that he does not foresee such a departure. "I don't see the USA leaving NATO," Rutte said, calling the speculation "absurd."[1][2]

The remarks come after weeks of heightened anxiety across European capitals following President Donald Trump's repeated threats to reconsider US membership in the nearly eight-decade-old defense bloc. Trump told Reuters in early April that he was "absolutely" considering trying to withdraw the US from NATO, criticizing allied nations for what he described as insufficient support during the war against Iran.[3][4]

items.title: Iran says no new talks until framework agreed

featured_image.name: Exclusive: Iranian official talks nuclear program with CNN

items.description:
Iran's Deputy Foreign Minister Saeed Khatibzadeh on Saturday dismissed US President Donald Trump's claims about enriched uranium, declaring that Tehran will not hand over its stockpiles to the United States and that no date has been set for a new round of negotiations. Speaking to journalists on the sidelines of the Antalya Diplomatic Forum in Turkey, Khatibzadeh said the Iranians were not ready for face-to-face talks because the American negotiating position had not changed.[1][2][3]

"Until we agree on the framework, we cannot set the date," Khatibzadeh told reporters, according to Reuters. His remarks came days after Trump said on April 16 that the United States was "very close" to a deal and that Iran had "agreed to almost everything," including handing over its enriched uranium stockpile.[4][1]

items.title: US says 21 ships turned back under Iran blockade

featured_image.name: 21 ships turned back to Iran since US blockade began, says ...

items.description: The United States Navy has compelled 21 vessels to reverse course since the start of a naval blockade on Iranian ports, US Central Command announced on Friday, as enforcement operations expanded into open waters and began disrupting Iranian oil shipments well beyond the Strait of Hormuz.

items.title: Egypt, Pakistan building framework for lasting US-Iran peace

featured_image.name: Saudi, Pakistani, Egyptian FMs to join Türkiye talks at ...

items.description:
Egypt's Foreign Minister Badr Abdelatty confirmed on Saturday that Egypt and Pakistan are working closely together on a framework to secure a lasting peace between the United States and Iran, as four regional powers intensify diplomacy ahead of a ceasefire deadline set to expire on April 22.[1]

Abdelatty said Egypt, Turkey, Pakistan, and Saudi Arabia are coordinating on a broader regional initiative aimed at preventing further escalation and building a post-conflict security arrangement. He stressed the need to protect Gulf nations and ensure the stability of energy markets, supply chains, and food security.[1]
